literal: At the beginning of Jianyi both were killed at Heyin.
idiomatic: In early Jianyi both were killed at Heyin.

literal: Shishu's younger brother Shishen was given in succession to his uncle Xinzhi.
idiomatic: Shishu's brother Shishen was adopted by his uncle Xinzhi.

literal: Shishen's younger brother Shilian, styled Jixiu, was Chief Clerk of the Pingbei Headquarters of Jianzhou.
idiomatic: Shishen's brother Shilian, styled Jixiu, was chief clerk of Jianzhou's pingbei headquarters.

literal: At the end of Yong'an Erzhu Shilong stormed and took the prefectural city; he was killed.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Shilong took Jianzhou at the end of Yong'an, Shilian was killed.

literal: Shilian's younger brother Shipei, styled Jiwei, in Wuding was General Who Pacifies the East and Retainer of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Shilian's brother Shipei, styled Jiwei, in Wuding was general who pacifies the east and Sizhou retainer.

literal: Xidao's younger brother Xiyue was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing for Outer Troops.
idiomatic: Xidao's brother Xiyue was gentleman of the masters of writing for outer troops.

literal: Li's younger brother Qilin was Palace Attendant Within the Hall and Scribe, transferred to Attending Censor.
idiomatic: Li's younger brother Qilin was palace attendant within the hall, then attending censor.

literal: At the beginning of Taihe he was Governor of Xinping.
idiomatic: In early Taihe he governed Xinping.

literal: His son Gaogui in Xiaochang was Legal Bureau Aide of the Eastern Garrison Headquarters of Yanzhou.
idiomatic: His son Gaogui in Xiaochang was legal aide on Yanzhou's eastern staff.

literal: Gaogui's son Cao, styled Zhongzhi, was lofty, simple, and had style; early he was known for scholarship and elegantly loved literature.
idiomatic: Gaogui's son Cao, styled Zhongzhi, was austere and stylish, famed early for learning and fond of letters.

literal: Cao served Wei as Concurrent Regular Attendant on an embassy to Liang.
idiomatic: Cao of Wei served as concurrent regular attendant on an embassy to Liang.

literal: When the envoy returned he was Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: On his return he became minister of justice.

literal: Qi Wenxiang as heir was very fond of women; Cui Jishu was in charge of matchmaking.
idiomatic: Wenxiang of Qi, as heir apparent, was licentious; Cui Jishu arranged his affairs.

literal: Xue Zhi's wife Yuan of the Registrar's office was beautiful in color; she was brought in and he wished to have relations with her.
idiomatic: He brought in Yuan, wife of Registrar Xue Zhi, intending to take her.

literal: Yuan spoke uprightly and also wept.
idiomatic: Yuan rebuked him sternly and wept.

literal: The heir sent Jishu to deliver her to the Court of Justice to punish her.
idiomatic: The heir had Jishu send her to justice for punishment.

literal: Cao said: "The Minister of Justice guards the Son of Heaven's law; he must know the crime."
idiomatic: Cao said, "Justice guards the emperor's law—we must know the charge."

literal: " The heir was angry, summoned Cao, ordered the ring of the blade to strike him, and again ordered conviction.
idiomatic: The heir raged, had him beaten with a sword-ring, and demanded a verdict.

literal: Cao to the end did not bend; then he reproached him orally.
idiomatic: Cao never yielded and rebuked him to his face.

literal: Later he was transferred to Censor in Chief.
idiomatic: He was later made censor in chief.

literal: In Tianbao he died as Director Within the Hall of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he died as director within the hall of the masters of writing.

literal: His son Kongzhang in Wuping died as Governor of Gaoyang.
idiomatic: His son Kongzhang died in Wuping as governor of Gaoyang.

literal: Gaogui's younger brother Mengyuan held the post of Court Gentleman for the Dynasty.
idiomatic: Gaogui's brother Mengyuan was a court gentleman for the dynasty.

literal: Mengyuan's son Gaizhi held the post of Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
idiomatic: Mengyuan's son Gaizhi was minister of the imperial granaries.

literal: Gaizhi's son Shuang, styled Kaiming.
idiomatic: Gaizhi's son Shuang, styled Kaiming.

literal: In youth clever and keen; at nine he entered study; each day he recited more than two thousand words.
idiomatic: Clever as a boy, at nine he recited over two thousand characters a day.

literal: Yang Zunyan, Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing of Qi, saw him and marveled, saying: "The Lu clan always produces men."
idiomatic: Yang Zunyan, Qi vice minister of the masters of writing, said in wonder, "The Lus never run dry of talent."

literal: " He served Qi as Secretariat Vice Minister.
idiomatic: He served Qi as secretariat vice minister.

literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou heard his name and with Yang Xiuzhi, Yuan Shude, and others alike was summoned into the Pass.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, Zhou's emperor summoned him with Yang Xiuzhi and Yuan Shude into the Pass.

literal: Many brought heavy baggage; Shuang alone loaded several thousand scrolls of books.
idiomatic: Others hauled valuables; Shuang brought only thousands of scrolls.

literal: Reaching Chang'an he was appointed Upper Gentleman for Proclamation.
idiomatic: In Chang'an he was made upper gentleman for proclamation.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was repeatedly promoted to Crown Prince Reader; with Left Heir Apparent Yuwen Kai and others he compiled seventy scrolls of Records of the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Under Sui he rose to crown prince reader and with Yuwen Kai compiled seventy scrolls of Eastern Palace records.

literal: The court because of his broad learning and eloquence, whenever Chen people reached the border, always ordered him to welcome and comfort them.
idiomatic: His learning and tongue made him the court's choice to greet Chen envoys at the border.

literal: He died in office; posthumously awarded Upper Equal in Rank and Governor of Xuanzhou.
idiomatic: He died in office, posthumously upper equal in rank and governor of Xuanzhou.

literal: His son Fayin, keen in learning with family style, on first appointment was Gentleman for Reception.
idiomatic: His son Fayin, quick-witted and true to the family trade, began as gentleman for reception.

literal: At first when Shuang was reader he often memorialized to Emperor Wen: "The crown prince's sons have no fine names; I ask according to the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals to establish new names."
idiomatic: As reader, Shuang asked Wen to rename the crown prince's sons by Spring and Autumn precedent.

literal: " The emperor followed this.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

literal: When the crown prince was deposed the emperor pursued anger at Shuang, saying: "My grandsons' names—would I not understand them myself?"
idiomatic: When the crown prince fell, Wen raged at Shuang: "Did I need him to name my grandsons?"

literal: Lu Shuang is so meddlesome!
idiomatic: Lu Shuang meddled once too often!

literal: Inciting Yong also began with this man.
idiomatic: He also stirred up Yong.

literal: Though his person is gone, descendants should all be screened and dismissed, never counted among the ranks for life.
idiomatic: Though dead, his line should be erased from office forever.

literal: " Fayin in the end was punished by removal of name.
idiomatic: Fayin was struck from the rolls.

literal: Yuan He, a native of Ledu in Xiping, was son of Tufa Rutan, self-styled King of Hexi.
idiomatic: Yuan He of Ledu in Xiping was son of Tufa Rutan, the self-styled King of Hexi.

literal: Rutan was destroyed by Qifu Chitan; He fled from Ledu to Wei.
idiomatic: When Chitan of Qifu destroyed Rutan, He fled to Wei from Ledu.

literal: He had grand appearance and was skilled in bearing and deportment.
idiomatic: He was imposing and graceful in manner.

literal: Taiwu had long heard his name.
idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu had long known his name.

literal: When he saw him he valued his quick wit in debate and enfeoffed him Marquis of Xiping.
idiomatic: Meeting him, the emperor prized his wit and made him Marquis of Xiping.

literal: He said: "You and I share one source; because of events the surnames were divided; now you may take the surname Yuan."
idiomatic: He said, "We share one origin; take the surname Yuan."

literal: " He followed in striking the rebel Hu Bailong and again campaigned against the Tujing Hu; in both he was first to ascend and break the lines.
idiomatic: He helped crush Bailong and the Tujing Hu, always first over the wall.

literal: For merit his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
idiomatic: For merit he became General Who Pacifies the West.

literal: Taiwu campaigned on Liangzhou and used him as native guide, asking plans of attack and battle.
idiomatic: On the Liangzhou campaign Taiwu used him as guide and asked his battle plan.

literal: He said: "Outside Guzang are four divisions of Xianbei, each a support for it, yet all are my grandfather's old men."
idiomatic: He said, "Four Xianbei divisions outside Guzang support the city, but they are my grandfather's old followers."

literal: I wish before the army to proclaim the state's prestige and trust; they will surely lead one another to request surrender.
idiomatic: Let me proclaim the dynasty's authority—they will surrender in chains.

literal: Once outer support has submitted, then attack its lone city; taking it will be like turning the palm.
idiomatic: Once allies fall away, the lone city will fall at a touch.

literal: " The emperor said: "Good."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Good."

literal: " He then sent He to summon and comfort; more than thirty thousand households submitted.
idiomatic: He sent He to win them; thirty thousand households came in.

literal: When they besieged Guzang, thereby without outer concern they could concentrate force to attack it.
idiomatic: Besieging Guzang without outside interference, the army could strike with full force.

literal: When Liangzhou was pacified, for merit his rank was advanced to Duke of Xiping.
idiomatic: When Liangzhou fell he was raised to Duke of Xiping.

literal: He again followed campaigns against the Rouran, struck the Tujing Hu of Wucheng, and campaigned against the bandits of Gai Wu; in all he had merit and was appointed Regular Attendant.
idiomatic: More campaigns against Rouran, Tujing Hu, and Gai Wu won him regular attendant.

literal: Following the imperial carriage to the river he was Grand General of the Vanguard; he was good at comforting soldiers and moreover had stratagems to gauge the enemy and secure victory.
idiomatic: At the Yangzi he led the vanguard, comforted the troops, and outthought the enemy.

literal: He as a man was bold and resolute; whenever he met strong bandits he would himself spring to attack; the emperor deeply admonished him.
idiomatic: Bold to a fault, he threw himself at every strong foe until the emperor warned him.

literal: He's original name was Poqiang; in this campaign the emperor said to him: "When a man establishes a name he should preserve its reality—how can it be excessive?"
idiomatic: Born Poqiang, he was told in this war, "A name should fit the deed—yours is too grand."

literal: " He was given the name He.
idiomatic: He was renamed He.

literal: He was appointed Director Within the Hall of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He became director within the hall of the masters of writing.

literal: The Prince of Nan'an Yu was killed by Zong Ai; He mustered forbidden troops, quieted and restrained inside and outside, and with Lu Li, Vice Minister of the Southern Masters of Writing, decided the plan and supported and established Wencheng.
idiomatic: When Zong Ai murdered Prince Yu of Nan'an, He rallied the guard, steadied the palace with Lu Li, and enthroned Wencheng.

literal: He ordered Li and Liu Ni to gallop to the park to welcome him; He in camp was inner responder.
idiomatic: He sent Li and Liu Ni to the park to fetch the heir while he held the camp.

literal: Before long Li embraced Wencheng and came alone on one horse.
idiomatic: Soon Li arrived alone on horseback carrying the boy emperor.

literal: When he took the throne He had strength in it.
idiomatic: He had done much to place him on the throne.

literal: For merit in fixing the plan his rank was advanced to Prince of Xiping.
idiomatic: For fixing the succession he was made Prince of Xiping.

literal: When rewards were distributed to the hundred officials, an edict ordered He to take as he wished; he declined on the grounds that the south was not yet subject and the north of the Han not yet submissive—the treasury should not be brought to want.
idiomatic: At the general reward he was told to take what he wished but refused, saying the treasury must stay full while north and south were still unconquered.

literal: They firmly made him take; he took only one horse of the Rong.
idiomatic: Pressed again, he took only one frontier horse.

literal: At the time judging criminal cases was much excessive.
idiomatic: Justice then ran to excess.

literal: He memorialized: "According to the code, in families guilty of rebellion, though descendants were raised in other clans they were pursued back and put to death—this was to cut off the criminal kind and display the guilt of great treason."
idiomatic: He wrote that rebel clans—even children raised elsewhere—were hunted down to extirpate traitors, unlike mere bandits.

literal: For those who were robbers deserving execution, brothers, sons, and nephews beyond distant roads and separated by passes and fords were all not implicated.
idiomatic: Yet robbers' kin far beyond the passes were spared—a deliberate distinction.

literal: I reflect that the former court's intent in making the code was that not sharing the plot was not a crime of cutting off the kind, so they specially granted the edict of not dying.
idiomatic: The old code meant non-conspirators were not of the traitor's kind and deserved mercy.

literal: If under thirteen years, the family's chief villain, it was beyond their reckoning.
idiomatic: Children under thirteen could not be held to account for the plot.

literal: Your servant foolishly thinks their lives may be spared and they be confiscated into government service.
idiomatic: He urged sparing such lives and enrolling them as government slaves.

literal: " The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

literal: He went out as Governor of Jizhou and his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Longxi.
idiomatic: He went out to Jizhou and was made Prince of Longxi.

literal: Having received the appointment, he memorialized: "Your servant hears that among what men treasure, nothing is treasured like life;
idiomatic: On taking office he wrote: "Of all treasures, life is dearest;

literal: among those thick in virtue, nothing is thicker than sparing death.
idiomatic: among mercies, none greater than sparing the condemned;

literal: Yet crimes deserving death are hard to pardon entirely.
idiomatic: yet capital crimes cannot all be forgiven.

literal: Weigh their light and heavy; some may be pitied and comforted.
idiomatic: Still, weight and mercy may leave room for pity.

literal: Now fierce bandits wander as souls in the north; crafty foes hold peril in the south; those on the borders still need garrison defense.
idiomatic: Fierce foes haunt north and south; the borders still need men.

literal: Your servant foolishly thinks that apart from great treason and bare-handed killing, those whose crimes are embezzlement, theft, and negligent faults that should enter death may all have life spared and be banished to guard the frontier.
idiomatic: Save outright treason and murder, let embezzlers and thieves live as frontier guards.

literal: Then bodies already cut off would again receive the grace of birth;
idiomatic: Men marked for death would live again;

literal: households of corvée would gradually receive the benefit of rest.
idiomatic: corvée households would breathe easier.

literal: The transformation of putting away punishments would nearly lie herein.
idiomatic: Thus punishment might nearly disappear.

literal: " The emperor gladly accepted it; afterward those entering death were all spared death and banished to the frontier.
idiomatic: The emperor embraced the plan; thereafter capital sentences became exile.

literal: After a long time the emperor told the ministers: "In the past Yuan He urged me to spare all death penalties and move them to fill the northern frontier garrisons."
idiomatic: Long after, the emperor told his ministers how He had urged sparing the condemned for the northern garrisons.

literal: From then until now, those living a year are quite not few.
idiomatic: Since then the lives saved each year were many.

literal: The principle of saving lives being much, the frontier garrison troops had benefit.
idiomatic: Saving so many lives also strengthened the frontier.

literal: If every man were like He, I facing all under Heaven—what again would I worry about!
idiomatic: If all my men were like He, what should I fear under heaven!

literal: " The ministers all said: "Without a loyal minister one could not advance this plan; without a sage and enlightened ruler one could not accept these words."
idiomatic: The ministers said only a loyal minister proposes such a plan and only a sage accepts it.

literal: When He came to the province, he judged cases by sentiment, simplified corvée, was pure, sparing, and broad, and deeply won people's hearts.
idiomatic: As governor he judged by the facts, eased corvée, lived sparely, and won deep loyalty.

literal: At the time a villain of Wuyi commandery, Shi Hua, reported the monk Daoke plotting rebellion with He; the offices reported it.
idiomatic: A Wuyi scoundrel accused monk Daoke and He of plotting rebellion.

literal: Wencheng said: "He assuredly has not this."
idiomatic: Wencheng said, "He would never do that."

literal: " He then finely added interrogation and examination; Hua indeed led to false accusation.
idiomatic: A careful inquiry proved Hua's frame-up.

literal: He then sent an envoy to comfort and encourage him.
idiomatic: The emperor sent He words of comfort.

literal: The emperor turned to those at his side and said: "He is loyal and sincere—yet he still meets false slander; for those not like this, can one not be cautious!"
idiomatic: He told his attendants, "If even loyal He is slandered, how careful must lesser men be!"
